subject: Discovery recap & benchmark asks — LumenAI evaluation
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@lumenai.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & next steps — Redwood vs on-prem vLLM/TGI evaluation

Hi Alex / Priyanka —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from my side so we have alignment before we wire up the benchmark run:

Pain points you mentioned:
- High p50 latency for interactive summarization (current median ~300ms for 512-token flows).
- Large bursty traffic during business hours causing queueing on your self-hosted vLLM cluster.
- Cost unpredictability and engineering time spent tuning quantization and batching heuristics.
- Concern about data residency and audit logs for model access.

Current stack you shared:
- Serving: self-managed vLLM on EC2 (Nvidia A10G), custom autoscaler, local filesystem KV cache.
- Evaluation harness: internal Python scripts + a static prompt set (~4k promps).
- Integrations: embeddings sent to managed vector db (hosted), downstream app in GCP.

Success criteria you outlined for the bake-off:
1) Latency: p50 < 120ms and p95 < 350ms for 512-token interactive prompt set.
2) Throughput: sustain 25 concurrent streams with <5% error rate.
3) Cost: comparable or lower 3-month unit cost for production traffic (we'll use projected 1M tokens/day baseline).
4) Quality parity: outputs align with your internal acceptance tests (we'll run your 500-case rubric).
5) Security/compliance: SOC 2 evidence + audit log access or Private deployment option.

What Redwood will provide next (deliverables):
- Benchmark spec (attached redwood-bench-specs.xlsx) with exact model variants, input distributions, and measurement scripts.
- A temporary test tenant and API keys for Redwood Hosted + Dedicated (if you want to test iso hardware).
- A sample config for running the same harness against our Hosted API and against a self-managed Redwood Private image (if you prefer on-prem).
- A short mutual-action-plan doc outlining timeline, owners, and acceptance sign-offs (attached).

Requested from LumenAI to start the run:
- Confirm the 500-case rubric (share as a CSV) and the subset of prompts you want prioritized.
- Provide a lightweight sample of production traffic characteristics (token lengths, concurrency patterns).
- Point person on infra to set up network access for Dedicated/Private trial: Priyanka?

Proposed immediate next steps:
- You confirm the rubric and a target date for a two-day benchmark run (we suggested Aug 3–4).
- Technical deep-dive with your infra team to discuss connectivity and KV cache migration (propose Jul 27 @ 10am PT).
- Redwood to send bench spec + test tenant by EOD tomorrow.

If that looks right, I’ll open a HubSpot deal and add the timeline. Appreciate the clarity today — excited to help you compare realistic options to your current vLLM setup and to TGI/cloud endpoints.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-bench-specs.xlsx, mutual-action-plan.md
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@lumenai.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyanka Rao <priya@lumenai.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps — Redwood vs on-prem vLLM/TGI evaluation

Vanessa —

Thanks for the crisp recap. Quick clarifications from our side:
- The 500-case rubric exists; I’ll drop a CSV in the Drive link you shared by tomorrow morning.
- Priyanka will be our infra lead for the Dedicated/Private trial — she can join the Jul 27 deep-dive.
- For cost comparisons, can Redwood provide an estimated $/1M token figure for Hosted and an estimated $/1M token for a Dedicated baseline (including reserved capacity amortization)? We need a ballpark in the next week to align finance.

A couple of redlines on acceptance: to consider Redwood a viable replacement we need a clear fall-back/fallback-window plan (what happens if Dedicated capacity saturates) and a runbook for KV cache warm-up to avoid cold-start tail latencies.

We’re comfortable with Aug 3–4 for a two-day run as long as we have the bench spec and test tenant by Jul 23.

Appreciate it — I’ll confirm rubric upload tomorrow.

—Alex
Senior Engineering Manager, LumenAI
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@lumenai.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 08:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps — Redwood vs on-prem vLLM/TGI evaluation

Alex —

Thanks — adding the numbers you asked for. Ballpark estimates (will refine after we see the actual token distribution):
- Redwood Hosted (curated open models, multi-tenant): ~$95 per 1M tokens for your profile (interactive + embedding mix).
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved A10G-equivalent pools, included autoscaling): ~$45 per 1M tokens amortized across a 12-month commit (varies with commit size).
- Note: self-hosted on vLLM has lower nominal infra spend but higher engineering ops cost and variance due to tuning; we’ll show a 3-month TCO in the bench report.

Regarding fallbacks: our standard policy for Dedicated customers is cross-region fallback to a compatible model variant (graceful degradation to a smaller quantized model) with auto-routing by policy. We’ll include explicit SLOs and escalation steps in the MAP.

On KV cache warm-up: we’ll provide a sample warm-up script and an approach for prefix caching that reduces cold-start p95 by ~40% in our tests; we’ll include that in the bench spec.

I’ve scheduled the Jul 27 technical deep-dive with Priyanka and sent a calendar invite. We’ll send the bench spec + temporary keys by Jul 23 EOD.

Rafael
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
